questions.question: The given bar graph shows the sales of cars from six branches of a dealer B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, during two consecutive years 2018 and 2019. Blue color corresponds to the year 2018 and the light blue color corresponds to the year 2019. The total sale of cars from all the branches in the year 2018 is what percentage less than the total sales of cars from all the branches in the year 2019? (correct to one decimal place)
questions.questionHtml:
The given bar graph shows the sales of cars from six branches of a dealer B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, during two consecutive years 2018 and 2019. Blue color corresponds to the year 2018 and the light blue color corresponds to the year 2019.

The total sale of cars from all the branches in the year 2018 is what percentage less than the total sales of cars from all the branches in the year 2019? (correct to one decimal place)
questions.solution:
Total number of cars in 2018 

80 + 75 + 95 + 85 + 75 + 70 = 480

Total number of cars in 2019

110 + 105 + 65 + 95 + 95 + 80 = 550

Different between 2018 and 2019 

550 - 480 = 70 

Percentage less than the total sales cars from all the branches in the 2019 

⇒ \(\frac{{70}}{{550}} \times 100\)

⇒ 12.7

questions.question: The given bar graph shows the imports and export (in crore Rs.) of steel for 5 years from 2014 to 2018. What is the ratio of average export to average import over the five years?
questions.questionHtml:
The given bar graph shows the imports and export (in crore Rs.) of steel for 5 years from 2014 to 2018.

What is the ratio of average export to average import over the five years?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Total import in five years = 350 + 380 + 420 + 450 + 580 = Rs.2180 crores

Average import in five years = 2180/5 = Rs.436 crores

Total export in five years = 400 + 420 + 550 + 480 + 620 = Rs.2470 crores

Average export in five years = 2470/5 = Rs.494 crores

Required ratio = 494 : 436 = 247 : 218

∴ the ratio of average export to average import over the five years is 247 : 218.

questions.question: The wages of workers (W1, W2, W3, W4, W5, W6) for different tasks (T1, T2, T3) are given What is the difference in average wages per worker for task T1 and task T3?
questions.questionHtml:
The wages of workers (W1, W2, W3, W4, W5, W6) for different tasks (T1, T2, T3) are given

What is the difference in average wages per worker for task T1 and task T3?
questions.solution:
Sum of wages for T3 = 23, Number of workers = 6

The average for T3 = \(\frac{\text{Sum of Wages}}{Total\space workers}\) = \(\frac{23}{6}\)

Sum of wages for T1 = 21, Number of workers = 6

The average for T1= \(\frac{\text{Sum of Wages}}{Total\space workers}\) = \(\frac{21}{6}\)

Difference between them = Average for T3 - Average for T1 = \(\frac{23}{6}-\frac{21}{6}=\frac{2}{6}=\frac{1}{3} \)

⇒ [(320 – 280)/280 × 100]

⇒ 14.28%

The production of sugar in 2015 = 320

The production of sugar in 2016 = 380

The percentage increase in the production of sugar in 2016 as compared to that in its preceding year 2015 

⇒ [(380 – 320)/320 × 100]

⇒ (60/320 × 100)

⇒ 18.75%

The production of sugar in 2016 = 380

The production of sugar in 2017 = 400

The percentage increase in the production of sugar in 2017 as compared to that in its preceding year 2016

⇒ [(400 – 380)/380 × 100]

⇒ (20/380 × 100)

⇒ 5.26%

The production of sugar in 2017 = 400

The production of sugar in 2018 = 440

The percentage increase in the production of sugar in 2018 as compared to that in its preceding year 2017

⇒ [(440 – 400)/400 × 100]

⇒ (40/400 × 100)

⇒ 10%

The production of sugar in 2018 = 440

The production of sugar in 2019 = 480

The percentage increase in the production of sugar in 2019 as compared to that in its preceding year 2018

⇒ [(480 – 440)/440 × 100]

⇒ (40/440 × 100)

⇒ 9.09%

∴ The increase in the production of sugar as compared to that in its preceding year between 8% and 10% in 2019

questions.question: Study the given histogram that shows the marks obtained by students in an examination and answer the question that follows. questions.question: Given bar graph shows, total expenditure and the gross receipts of a company (in Rs. crores). Study the graph and answer the question that follows: In order to make a profit of 20% what should have been the gross receipts (in crore Rs.) in 1995-96, if the total expenditure remained the same?
questions.questionHtml:
Given bar graph shows, total expenditure and the gross receipts of a company (in Rs. crores). Study the graph and answer the question that follows:

 

In order to make a profit of 20% what should have been the gross receipts (in crore Rs.) in 1995-96, if the total expenditure remained the same?
questions.solution:
Given:

Expenditure in the year 1995-96 = 5500

Profit % = 20%

Formula used:

Profit % = (Profit/Expenditure) × 100

Profit = Recipient - Expenditure

Calculation:

∵ Profit % = (Profit/Expenditure) × 100

⇒ 20 = (profit/5500) × 100

⇒ 20 = Profit/55

⇒ Profit = 55 × 20 = 1100

∴ Receipts = Expenditure + Profit

⇒ Receipts = 5500 + 1100

⇒ Receipts = 6600

∴ The correct answer is 6600.

questions.question: Study the given graph and answer the question that follows. The total production of paper by company B in 2015 and 2017 to 2019 was what percentage less than 90% of the total production of paper by company A in 2014 to 2019 (correct to one decimal place)?

The total production of paper by company B in 2015 and 2017 to 2019 was what percentage less than 90% of the total production of paper by company A in 2014 to 2019 (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Total production of Company B in 2015 and 2017 to 2019

⇒ 70 + 150 + 180 + 120 = 520 lakh tonnes

Total production of Company A in 2014 to 2019

⇒ 70 + 90 + 120 + 140 + 130 + 150 = 700 lakh tonnes

90% of the total production of Company A

⇒ 700 × 90% = 630 lakh tonnes

% = (630 - 520)/630 × 100% ≈ 17.5%

∴ The total production of paper by company B in 2015 and 2017 to 2019 was 17.5% less than 90% of the total production of paper by company A in 2014 to 2019.

questions.question: Study the given histogram that shows the marks obtained by students in an examination and answer the question that follows. If the total number of students is represented as a pie chart, then the central angle corresponding to students whose marks are more than 250 but less than 300 is? (correct to the nearest degree)
questions.questionHtml:
Study the given histogram that shows the marks obtained by students in an examination and answer the question that follows.

If the total number of students is represented as a pie chart, then the central angle corresponding to students whose marks are more than 250 but less than 300 is?

(correct to the nearest degree)
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Total number of students = 30 + 45 + 60 + 35 + 40 +35

⇒ Total number of students = 245

And students whose marks are more than 250 but less than 300 = 60

But 245 students represents 360°

⇒ 1 student = 360° /245

⇒ 60 students = (360° /245) × 60

⇒ 60 students = 88.16°

∴ The nearest value for students corresponding to 250 or more but lesser than 300 is 88° .

questions.question: The given bar chart shows the number of students in a class who have secured marks in three ranges: >= 75%, 60% - 74% and <60% What is the ratio of percentages of boys and girls who got marks from 60% to 74%?
questions.questionHtml:
The given bar chart shows the number of students in a class who have secured marks in three ranges: >= 75%, 60% - 74% and <60%

What is the ratio of percentages of boys and girls who got marks from 60% to 74%?
questions.solution:
Given:

Number of boys whose marks range >= 75% = 12

Number of boys whose marks range 60% - 74% = 45

Number of boys whose marks range <60% = 8

Number of girls whose marks range >= 75% = 7

Number of girls whose marks range 60% - 74% = 53

Number of girls whose marks range <60% = 5

Concept used:

Using the concept of percentage.

Calculation:

Total number of boys = 12 + 45 + 8 = 65

Total number of girls = 7 + 53 + 5 = 65

Percentages of boys who got marks from 60% to 74% = (45/65) × 100

⇒ The required percentage = 69.23%

Percentages of girls who got marks from 60% to 74% = (53/65) × 100

⇒ The required percentage = 81.53%

So, The ratio of percentages of boys and girls who got marks from 60% to 74% = (69.23%)/(81.53%) = 69.23 ∶  81.53

∴ The ratio of percentages of boys and girls who got marks from 60% to 74% is 69.23 ∶  81.53.
